card.name: "Should be" before considered
card.fires_on: The word "be" right after "should" (or "should always") when a sentence about a possibility or factor is about to say it "should be considered". It is most common in overdose-management text, e.g. "the possibility of multiple drug involvement should be".

modes.label: Possibility should be considered
modes.description: "be" after "should" following a sentence subject like "the possibility of multiple drug involvement", in overdose sections.
modes.example: The possibility of multiple drug involvement should<< be>> considered. Establish and maintain an airway

modes.label: Other should-be-reviewed statements
modes.description: "be" after "should" where a monitoring or reconsideration verb follows.
modes.example: the signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity should<< be>> carefully monitored.

modes.label: Infinitive "to" before consider
modes.description: A rarer case: "to" right before a verb of considering, in a committee description.
modes.example: established an Environmental Audit Committee<< to>> consider how policies and programmes of Government Departments

card.writes: It pushes toward words like consider, critics and criticism, i.e. the idea of weighing or reviewing something.
card.plain: It fires on "be" in "should be" when the next word is likely "considered".
